sentences.text:
By way of present appeal, the appellant herein has challenged the judgment dated 27.03.2017 and order on the point of sentence dated 30.03.2017 passed by the then learned ACMM-II, PHC, New Delhi vide which the appellant/accused was held guilty for commission of offences punishable under sections 16(1A) r/w Section 7 of PFA Act for violation of Section 2(ia) (j) and (m) of PFA Rules 1955 and was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for one year and to pay a fine of Rs. 30,000/-
and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for 15 days.
Benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C, if any, applicable was also given to him.

sentences.text: That the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, hence, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned by the learned trial court vide order dated 08.11.2002 to face trial.

- After filing appearance appellant/accused adopted the procedure available as per the statute ;
pre-charge evidence was recorded ; and on the basis of testimony of prosecution witnesses, charge was framed CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 3 of 9 against the accused to which he pleaded not guilty ; thereafter statement of accused was recorded and after seeking opportunity to lead DE, no witness was examined or produced ; final arguments were heard and accused was held guilty by the learned trial court observing that it stands established by prosecution beyond reasonable doubt that the accused had sold adulterated food in violation of Section 2(ia),(j) and (m) of PFA Act read with Rules 23,28 and 29 of the PFA Rules and has committed the offence punishable under Section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act and was thus convicted for the said offences by the learned trial court.
- In the order on quantum of sentence, appellant was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for one year and to pay a fine of Rs. 30,000/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for 15 days for offence punishable u/s 16(1A) r/w Section 7 of PFA Act, 1954 .
5.(I) The appellant has assailed the judgment and order on sentence passed by the learned trial court by urging various grounds.
5.(II)

sentences.text: However, during the course of argument on 06.10.2021, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant does not wish to contest the present petition on merits, and the benefit of new legislation be given to the appellant; in this regard, on behalf of the appellant, an affidavit was also filed, mentioning that he is not challenging the merits of the case/ conviction decided by the learned trial court vide judgment dated 27.03.2017, and is confining it limited to the quantum of sentence only as awarded to him vide order dated 30.03.2017, and prayed that a lenient view be taken against him by giving him the benefit of New Legislation FSSAI.

6. It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that on the date of pronouncement of judgment/order on sentence, the PFA Act, 1954 was CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 4 of 9 repealed and new act had come into operation.

entities.text: CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 4 of 9
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is stated that the court should give benefit of the new legislation to the accused vide which the punishment provided under the old act has been diluted to a considerable extent, and that the offence for which the accused/appellant has been convicted now falls under the category of "Unsafe Food" punishable under section 59(1) of the new Act i.e Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called FSSAI) punishable upto six months and fine of upto Rs. One lac only, and the minimum sentence provided in the earlier act has also been done away with.
7.

It was argued by learned counsel for the appellant/convict that appellant is senior citizen aged about 66 years, suffering from paralysis and various ailments and thereby is not able to move and follow his daily routine work; that he has no source of income and the shop in question herein was also closed permanently way back about 15 years ago; that as of now due to his financial as well as Madan Lal Dawar vs Food Inspector on 8 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146237763/
3 precarious medical condition, he is totally dependent upon his daughter with whom he is residing presently; that appellant has clean antecedents, not involved in any other case of similar nature or otherwise.
7.1

entities.text: Madan Lal Dawar vs Food Inspector

sentences.text: Further, it was submitted that the case pertains to the year 2002, the appellant/accused has faced the trial of almost 20 years, which by itself is a sufficient punishment in light of the fact that the hardship faced by the appellant during the said period has caused a great mental agony and stress not only to him but his entire family.

It is also stated that now a days special circumstances exists due to outbreak of pandemic of Covid- 19 and there are chances of appellant being infected with virus in case imprisonment of sentence is awarded to him, and thereby it is prayed that a lenient view be taken against him in the light of the provisions of law under the new Act.
CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 5 of 9 7.2

sentences.text: In support of his submissions qua the benefit of new legislation, learned counsel for appellant has relied upon the judgment of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No. 214 and 215 of 2016, vide order dated 10.03.2016, as corrected vide order dated 17.03.2016, as reported in 2016 (1) FAC 203 ) of Hon'ble Supreme Court and earlier judgment T Barai Vs. Henry 1983 ( ) SCC 177. 7.3

entities.text: Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No. 214 and 215 of 2016
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Per contra,
learned SPP, strongly opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel by addressing that the sentencing cannot be done under new Act since the definition of many offences have changed in the new Act including this particular offence of which appellant/accused is charged.
Definition of major offences like "adulteration" and "misbranding" have been changed.
Now FSSAI has definitions of "substandard food", "food containing extraneous matter" "unsafe food" and misbranded food".
Due to this reason, the ingredients have changed and thus there is no way in which the old offences could be related to new offences.
7.4 The application of Nemi Chand Judgment (supra), the same is based on the old judgment i.e. T Barai ( Supra) of Hon'ble Supreme Court.

The relevant portion of the T Barai Judgment is as follows :
- (Para 25) It is settled both on authority and principle that when a later statute again describes an offence created by an earlier statute and imposes a different punishment or varies the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by implication in Michell Vs.
Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80 Lord Campbell put the matter thus :
- "It is well settled rule of construction that, if a later statute again describes an offence created by a former statute and affixes a different punishment, varying the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by the later statute see also Smith Vs.
Benabo ( 1937) 1 ALL ER 523 : ( 1997) 1 CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 6 of 9 KB 518: 156 LT 194"

Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80

- In Regina Vs. Youle ( 1861) 158 ER 311,315-16 : LT 299 : 9 WR 637 Martin B. said in the oft-quoted passage :

4 - If a statute deals with a particular class of offences, and a subsequent Act is passed which deals with precisely the same offence, and a different punishment is imposed by the later Act, I think that, in effect, the legislature has declared that the new Act shall be substituted for the earlier Act."

sentences.text:
- The rule is however subject to the limitation contained in Article 20(1) against ex post facto law providing for a greater punishment and has also no application where the offence described in the later Act is not the same as in the earlier Act i.e. when the essential ingredients of the two offences are different.
- Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows :
- Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows :
- To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life, then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases.
7.5 - At this stage, Academic Reference can also be made to a letter dated 03.10.2017 issued by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, produced before the court during the proceedings.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Vide said letter the said authority, in the light of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's Case (supra) issued an advisory to the Commissioners of Food Safety/Officers incharge of Food Safety to dispose of the long CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 7 of 9 pending court cases filed under old PFA Act mainly concerning substandard and misbranding by imposing fine only.

entities.text: CA no. 65/2017 Madan Lal Dawar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7.6 - In view of the above discussion, it can be safely said that while considering on the point of sentence, in backdrop of the object and reasons of the new act and the intention of the legislature, the quantum of sentence so passed, in the interest of justice, can legally be considered under the new Act i.e. FSSAI, while deciding the present appeal.
8.

Thus, analyzing the facts of the case, taking note of the special circumstances of the appellant/convict as highlighted by his affidavit filed on record, and that no other previous or subsequent involvement is cited, and coupled with the the fact that appellant has faced the trial of almost 20 years, read in light of the above cited judgment and the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi titled as GNCT Vs.
Jagdish Tyagi dated 11.10.2017 in my considered view the convict/ appellant is entitled to the benefit of new legislation.

Accordingly, to meet the ends of justice, the sentence of the appellant as awarded by the learned trial court vide order dated 30.03.2017 sentencing him to undergo simple imprisonment for one year and to pay Madan Lal Dawar vs Food Inspector on 8 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146237763/
5 a fine of Rs.30,000/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for 15 days for offence punishable u/s 16(1A) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act,1954 for violation of Section 2(ia),(j) and (m) of PFA Act read with Rules 23,28 and 29 of the PFA Rules with benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C, if any, stands modified to the extent that- -instead of one year imprisonment appellant shall undergo TRC and shall pay a fine of Rs. 50,000/-
instead of Rs. 30,000/- as awarded to him by the learned trial court.
Sentence modified accordingly.
